## Why This Is Asked
Beginners must apply concrete security defaults to container specs, learn how policies gate PRs, and validate locally and in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- Kyverno policy syntax and testing
- CI gate integration in GitHub Actions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sec-context
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-sec-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job","CronJob"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must run as non-root with readOnlyRootFilesystem and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical dependency security skills in a real monorepo environment containing both JavaScript and Python services, along with understanding of license compliance policies.

## Key Concepts
- Integrating npm audit and pip-audit into CI pipelines
- Lightweight license allowlist enforcement
- Building a CI gate that blocks merges on CVEs or disallowed licenses
- Verification workflows for both local development and CI environments

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/dependency-security.yml
name: Dependency Security Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  security-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install Node dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Run npm audit
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
      
      - name: Run pip-audit
        run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Check licenses
        run: |
          npx license-checker --json > licenses.json
          # Script checks licenses against allowlist
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Kubernetes network security basics and CI gates using simple Bash checks. It also tests encoding a defensive posture with per-Namespace policies and simple allowlists. The candidate demonstrates crafting minimal, maintainable checks and integrating them into CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped policy enforcement
- GitHub Actions simple gate
- Local validation with kubectl dry-run

## Code Example
```bash
# check-netpol.sh (simplified)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR=${1:-manifests}
for ns in $(yq e '.kind=="Namespace"|.metadata.name' -N "$DIR" | sort -u); do
  if ! grep -R --quiet "NetworkPolicy" "$DIR/$ns" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Missing NetworkPolicy in namespace $ns"; exit 1
  fi
done
```

## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (example): OPA-based API access gate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapiaiaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAPIAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package k8sapiaiaccess
      violate["API access denied: identity not whitelisted"] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        identity := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["spire.identity"]
        not identity_in_allowlist(identity)
      }
      
      # allowlisted identities (simplified)
      identity_in_allowlist(id) {
        id == "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-spark
  annotations:
    spire.identity: "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: spark-sa
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod (no SPIRE identity)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-spark
spec:
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

- Deploy noncompliant pod; confirm admission denies with clear event reason.
